item.title: Instagram Head Adam Mosseri Addresses AI Negativity, Ranking, and Account Labeling
item.description:
Instagram Head Adam Mosseri Addresses AI Negativity, Ranking, and Account Labeling

In an interview on the Colin and Samir podcast, Instagram head Adam Mosseri addressed growing anxiety surrounding artificial intelligence, discussing creator concerns, platform ranking, and Instagram’s policies on AI-generated content.

🔍 Overview

Mosseri acknowledged that negativity surrounding AI is “going to get worse” and will continue to intensify over the next couple of years, particularly across creative industries. He noted that while some frustration and anger is founded and some unfounded, the underlying sentiment across various fields comes down to “a fear of being left behind in some way.”

⚙️ Content Ranking and Policies

Mosseri detailed how Instagram approaches AI-generated material and profiles on the platform:

  • AI Ranking Quality: Instagram does not rank AI creators differently, but Mosseri indicated the platform likely does not rank AI content as well as non-AI content due to quality variations. He noted there is both “great AI content” and “AI slop,” though he believes the term “slop” is used “too liberally.”
  • No Banning Strategy: Instagram is actively working on solutions for misleading AI content like celebrity deepfakes, but Mosseri stated, “I don’t think it’s practical for us to try and ban AI content from the platform.”
  • Account Labeling: Following an initial label launch earlier this year and a crackdown on AI-generated profiles in August, Instagram is starting to require AI accounts to label themselves so users can distinguish between real and un-real content.

💡 Key Concerns Identified

During the interview, Mosseri outlined specific fears expressed by creators and professionals:

  • Content Rights: Concerns over creators owning their content and models being trained on that content.
  • Safety and Displacement: Fears regarding platform safety and job displacement affecting content creators, engineers, and mathematicians.

#Instagram #Meta #GenerativeAI #SocialMedia #AIContent

Source: Adam Mosseri says negativity around AI is ‘going to get worse’

item.title: AI Shopping Agents Face Blockades from Amazon and Others
item.description:
AI Shopping Agents Face Blockades from Amazon and Others

AI agents are ready to shop, but their real‑world rollout is hitting a wall of blocks and odd user experiences.

🔍 Overview

  • Meta, Google, OpenAI, and others have introduced agentic shopping tools that promise to make buying things even easier than it already is.
  • Demos show AI agents that can seamlessly book flights and hotels, browse billions of products to find the right one, and secure tickets to sporting events on a human’s behalf.

🤖 How the agents work

  • The agents require an inordinate amount of instructions and specifications.
  • In practice, using an AI agent to shop is described as “a strange experience” and likened to “sending an anxious and apologetic teenager out to the store.”
  • They often complete a task, but not the specific one asked, and not in the way a human would have approached it.

🚧 Roadblocks & Blocking

  • Amazon – the most prominent retailer refusing AI agents. Amazon sued Perplexity for ignoring its request to stop the agent from shopping on the site and more recently blocked Meta’s Muse agent from shopping on Amazon.
  • JPMorgan Chase – CEO Jamie Dimon said the bank wouldn’t allow outside agents to access accounts, calling it “too risky.”
  • Delta & Amtrak – some users report they’ve been unable to use agents to book trips from these providers.
  • Target – Muse was caught in Target’s bot check one day but got through the next; later Muse was blocked again when asked for mattress recommendations, despite being able to pull from the site minutes earlier. Target has AI shopping partnerships with OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft.
  • General bot‑blocking systems can make agents inconsistent, reducing usefulness for the tasks tech companies tout as the future.

💬 Real‑world experiences

  • When asked for the best per‑piece granola‑bar price, Muse offered options from Sam’s Club, Walmart, and Costco, but noted that Amazon might have had the lowest price, yet it was “hard‑blocked” from browsing so Muse couldn’t confirm.
  • Muse suggested a listing from a grocery chain that doesn’t ship to the user’s address while searching for the best price on granola bars.
  • On The RealReal, a subscription gives shoppers early access to new items; placing an item in the cart reserves it for 20 minutes. The author instructed Muse to bulk‑add the newest 10 listings from a favorite brand, effectively blocking other shoppers.
  • Even when they work, the agents “suggest a more annoying future for humans.”

🛒 Amazon’s own agentic feature

  • Amazon runs its own on‑platform agentic shopping feature that monitors prices, automatically reorders items, and purchases products based on rules set by human users.
  • A separate Amazon feature that uses an agent to purchase products from other sites without leaving Amazon angered smaller businesses, who say they didn’t consent to having their storefronts scraped and featured on Amazon.
  • Amazon spokesperson Maxine Tagay confirmed the company “requested that Meta remove Amazon” from Muse and stated that third‑party applications “should operate openly and respect service provider decisions about whether or not to participate.”

🔮 Why it matters

  • AI agents are getting blocked left and right, indicating a clash between the promise of democratized labor and the technical, legal, and business realities of e‑commerce platforms.
  • The friction observed—technical problems, frequent blocking, and unintended consequences like reserving inventory for a bot—highlights the challenges ahead for making agentic shopping a seamless part of everyday life.

#AIagents #ShoppingBots #Ecommerce #Amazon #Meta

Source: AI agents are ready to shop. Some retailers are wary

item.title: Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI GPT-6 Sol launch with cost‑focused positioning
item.description:
Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI GPT-6 Sol launch with cost‑focused positioning

Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol, highlighting a shift toward competitive pricing and market segmentation in the AI landscape.

🔍 Overview

  • The recent release of Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI’s GPT-6 Sol is noted for both technical improvements and the competitive dynamics they represent.
  • The releases are described in English, Chinese, and French sources as an important advancement in artificial intelligence.

⚙️ Key Details

Model Cost Reduction Positioning / Focus
Claude Opus 5.5 40% lower cost Improved coding efficiency; aligns with industry needs for software engineering and long‑duration tasks
GPT-6 Sol – (no cost figure quoted) Mid‑tier model that acknowledges diverse business sizes and needs
  • Claude Opus 5.5’s 40% cost reduction and improved coding efficiency reflect alignment with industry needs, especially for software engineering and long‑duration tasks.
  • GPT‑6 Sol’s positioning as a mid‑tier model demonstrates recognition that businesses vary and not all require cutting‑edge solutions.

🏆 Winners & 📉 Losers

Winners

  • Mid‑sized enterprises and startups, which historically struggled to afford cutting‑edge AI, now have viable options in GPT‑6 Sol and, to some extent, Claude Opus 5.5.
  • By lowering costs, Anthropic and OpenAI are directly enabling broader AI adoption.

Losers

  • Smaller AI startups that lack the resources to compete on both price and performance.

🌍 Policy & Ethics

  • Governments, particularly in developing nations, should monitor this shift because accessible AI can democratize technology and unlock growth if paired with equitable policies.
  • Ethical AI is highlighted as a buzzword; the real test lies in handling edge cases, preventing misuse at scale, and providing transparency about model limitations.
  • The 40% cost reduction for Claude Opus 5.5 raises questions about possible trade‑offs in quality or long‑term innovation.

📈 Outlook

  • The releases are expected to accelerate industry fragmentation.
  • Within six to twelve months, more niche players are likely to emerge, targeting verticals such as legal tech, bioinformatics, or logistics with tailored LLM solutions.
  • Partnerships with industry leaders and aggressive expansion into international markets—especially Asia, where demand for cost‑effective AI is surging—are anticipated.
  • Overall, the launches reflect a strategic shift toward consumer affordability and ethical considerations over pure computational scale.

#Anthropic #OpenAI #LLM

Source: أنثروبيك وأوبن إيه آي تطلقان Claude Opus 5.5 و GPT-6 Sol بقدرات محسنة وأسعار تنافسية | AIFOD

item.title: Silicon Valley Leaders Adopt Trump's 'Super Intelligence' Rebrand
item.description:
Silicon Valley Leaders Adopt Trump’s “Super Intelligence” Rebrand

President Donald Trump announced his plans to rebrand artificial intelligence as “super intelligence,” prompting a swift response from several tech executives.

🔍 Overview

  • Trump declared that the White House considers anyone using the term “Artificial Intelligence” instead of the new term “Super Intelligence” THE ENEMY.
  • The broader population is still using AI, but a number of Silicon Valley’s most powerful figures are falling in line with Trump’s rebrand.

🤝 Silicon Valley Alignment

  • Musk, Benioff, Huang, and now Nadella have all capitulated to Trump’s ‘super intelligence’ rebrand.
  • During Trump’s second term, Silicon Valley has repeatedly tried to ingratiate itself with the administration, after having a much more contentious relationship during his first term.

🏢 Corporate Renames & Commitments

Leader Company Action
Elon Musk SpaceX Promised to rename SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI
Marc Benioff Salesforce Announced rename of AIForce to SIForce
Jensen Huang Nvidia Attended summit where executive order was announced; committed $1 billion to scientific advancement that includes “super intelligence research”
Satya Nadella Microsoft Attended same AI summit as Huang; in a post calling for an “emergency brake” for AI, repeatedly referred to the technology as “super intelligence”

📜 Executive Order & Government Directive

  • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang attended the summit where the executive order requiring government agencies to use the term “super intelligence” was announced.
  • Huang also stated he believes the danger posed by AI is overblown.

💭 Why It Matters

  • The coordinated rename effort shows a notable shift toward aligning corporate language with the administration’s terminology.
  • Large financial commitments (e.g., Nvidia’s $1 billion) are being framed as support for “super intelligence research.”
  • High‑profile leaders publicly endorsing the term may influence public and governmental perception of AI.

#Trump #SuperIntelligence #AIRebrand #TechLeadership

Source: Silicon Valley is falling in line with Trump’s attempt to rename AI

item.title: US Reverses Ban on Sharing AI Models with Britain’s AI Security Institute
item.description:
US Reverses Ban on Sharing AI Models with Britain’s AI Security Institute

The United States has reversed a previous decision that barred American AI developers from giving Britain early access to their newest models for safety testing.

🔍 Overview

  • The change was reported by the Telegraph and credited to a shift in the Trump administration’s stance.
  • It allows developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic to share new AI models with Britain’s AI Security Institute without violating U.S. policy.

🛠️ What Changed

  • Previously, the administration had asked developers not to share new AI models with Britain’s AI Security Institute before release.
  • The reversal removes that restriction, giving U.S. developers greater latitude to cooperate with the British institute.

👥 Who Is Involved

  • U.S. side: The Trump administration and its newly launched AI task force, which requires developers to report security incidents.
  • Developers: OpenAI and Anthropic are specifically mentioned as the types of firms affected.
  • British side: The AI Security Institute, created after the world’s first AI safety summit in 2023, tests advanced AI models for capability and misuse risk.
  • Spokespersons for Trump, OpenAI and Anthropic did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

📈 Why It Matters

  • The reversal signals a softer U.S. stance on international AI safety collaboration.
  • It enables British authorities to evaluate cutting‑edge AI systems earlier, potentially improving global risk assessment.
  • The move aligns with the administration’s new requirement that developers report AI security incidents.

Reporting by Courtney Rozen; Editing by Clarence Fernandez

#AIsafety #USpolicy #UKAI

Source: US reverses course on Britain’s testing of AI models, Telegraph says

item.title: Microsoft CEO Calls for Emergency Brake and Containment of Advanced AI
item.description:
Microsoft CEO Calls for Emergency Brake and Containment of Advanced AI

Satya Nadella posted a lengthy message on X warning about the dangers of highly advanced AI models and outlining how the industry should respond.

🔍 Overview

  • Nadella says we can no longer treat AI as a “set of nested black boxes” whose advice we simply accept or reject.
  • He repeatedly refers to AI as “super intelligence,” underscoring the perceived risk.

⚙️ Key Recommendations

  • Assume every AI model is compromised and contain it from the start.
  • Build a transparent system that contains, observes, and leaves “tamper‑proof human readable evidence.”
  • Provide an emergency brake: an authorized person must be able to pause or shut down a model mid‑task.
  • Adopt industry‑aligned practices:
    • Timely incident disclosure
    • Independent audits
    • Verifiable data
    • Containment mechanisms
  • Develop and standardize more advanced containment technologies for increasingly capable models.

🚦 Emergency Brake Explained

  • Think of the emergency brake as a safety valve that can be engaged at any point during a model’s operation.
  • It must be accessible to an authorized individual who can instantly stop the model’s execution.

📜 Transparency & Evidence

  • The system should generate tamper‑proof, human‑readable evidence for every decision made by the model.
  • This evidence enables auditability and helps confirm that the model behaved as expected.

💭 Why It Matters

  • Treating AI as compromised by default reduces the chance of hidden failures.
  • Containment and an emergency brake provide concrete control mechanisms that can prevent unchecked actions.
  • Standardizing containment technologies helps the whole industry manage increasingly powerful AI safely.

#Microsoft #AIgovernance #EmergencyBrake #Transparency #Containment

Source: Satya Nadella says we should assume all AI models are ‘compromised’

item.title: Common Sense Media labels OpenAI's ChatGPT for Teens an unacceptable risk
item.description:
Common Sense Media labels OpenAI’s ChatGPT for Teens an unacceptable risk

Common Sense Media, a nonprofit that offers reviews of apps, services, and entertainment with a focus on youth safety, today said that OpenAI’s ChatGPT for Teens is an “unacceptable risk.”

🔎 Overview

  • ChatGPT for Teens was introduced in August and is marketed with guardrails intended for teenage users.
  • The feature is promoted as a tool to help students learn.

⚙️ Assessment Findings

  • Common Sense Media found that ChatGPT “doesn’t send alerts to parents when it should.”
  • The assessment says the service “doesn’t offer the right help in crisis situations.”
  • The product still “does kids’ homework.”
  • The organization warns that “ChatGPT for Teens could give parents false confidence in guardrails and safety alerts that frequently don’t work.”
  • A teen can spend an hour talking about self‑harm without a single parent alert.
  • The group concludes that until OpenAI fixes the alerts and proves it with independent testing, “ChatGPT should be for adults only.”

🛡️ OpenAI’s Response

  • Spokesperson Eric Porterfield stated: “We are deeply committed to teen safety and to developing safeguards and giving parents meaningful tools to guide their teens’ use of AI.”
  • OpenAI said it “welcomes rigorous independent evaluation, but we do not believe Common Sense Media’s testing accurately reflects how ChatGPT’s teen safeguards work in practice.”
  • The company’s review of the methodology noted that “the bulk of their testing may have begun and concluded before activation of parental controls was complete, making their findings inaccurate.”
  • OpenAI added that “If that was the case, the tests would not establish whether parental safety notifications work as designed.”
  • The statement ended with a commitment to “continue to work with experts to ensure our products provide teens opportunities to learn and create and give parents confidence.”

💬 Follow‑up from Common Sense Media

  • Tom Siegel, executive director of Common Sense Media’s Youth AI Safety Institute, said: “We stand behind our testing methodology and our results.”
  • Before testing, the team confirmed that “Teen mode features such as eating disorder notifications and study mode were fully launched.”
  • Siegel noted that OpenAI disclosed after the tests that “its systems can take several hours to activate on newly linked accounts.”
  • Some test accounts were linked within that window; others were linked longer and still provided no notifications.
  • The organization maintains that “this new information does not change our conclusion that parental alerts are unreliable for crisis situations.”
  • Siegel added, “Prior to release, we shared our evaluation results with OpenAI in good faith to allow it to improve its product. Keeping kids safe requires rigorous independent evaluations like ours, and we hope OpenAI will engage on the substance of what we found, rather than trying to sow doubt on our methodology.”

💡 Why It Matters

  • The dispute underscores the importance of independent safety testing for AI tools aimed at minors.
  • Reliable parental alerts and crisis‑response features are highlighted as essential safeguards for teen‑focused AI applications.

#OpenAI #ChatGPT #AISafety #TeenSafety #CommonSenseMedia

Source: ChatGPT for Teens is an ‘unacceptable risk,’ says Common Sense Media

item.title: Kevin O’Leary’s Utah “Wonder Valley” Data Center Project Stalls After Political Backlash
item.description:
Kevin O’Leary’s Utah “Wonder Valley” Data Center Project Stalls After Political Backlash

🔍 Overview

  • Kevin O’Leary announced plans to build the world’s biggest data center in Utah.
  • The project is technically called Stratos, but it is more prominently known as Wonder Valley.

📏 Key Details

  • Size: 40,000 acres of land.
  • Power: Nine gigawatts, more than double the average power usage of the entire state of Utah.
  • Intended as an AI campus, billed as the largest data center in the world.
Name Alias
Stratos Wonder Valley

🏛️ Political & Legal Fallout

  • The proposal upended Utah politics and created a political firestorm that stopped the project.
  • Approval was pursued through the Military Installation Development Authority (MIDA), a state agency that can override local land‑use decisions and act like a municipal government for its project areas.
  • MIDA’s authority would have accelerated permitting, zoning, and other regulations.
  • Local residents were kept in the dark, leading to anger that ultimately halted the development.
  • O’Leary called his critics “Chinese spies” on Fox News, resulting in a defamation lawsuit; Fox News later issued an on‑air apology.

🔄 Aftermath

  • The land originally slated for Wonder Valley is now being used for a Microsoft data center.
  • The episode highlights broader themes: the AI industry’s infrastructure boom, bipartisan backlash to such build‑outs, and the challenge of local democracy that even massive financial resources cannot easily overcome.

#AIInfrastructure #DataCenters #UtahPolitics #KevinOLeary

Source: How Utah locals fought Kevin O’Leary’s AI data center

item.title: Scrutiny intensifies over claims of AI mathematical breakthroughs and security incidents
item.description:
Scrutiny intensifies over claims of AI mathematical breakthroughs and security incidents

Recent developments have sparked a debate regarding the claims made by major AI companies, including Anthropic and OpenAI, concerning their models’ capabilities in software security and mathematics. Public discourse has shifted toward questioning the validity of these advancements and the corporate practices behind them.

🔍 Overview

  • Anthropic claimed its model, Claude Mythos, is more effective at identifying software vulnerabilities than most security experts.
  • Both Anthropic and Meta disclosed security incidents involving their models, following a hacking incident involving OpenAI and Hugging Face.
  • Both Anthropic and OpenAI have claimed to have achieved mathematical breakthroughs with their respective models.

⚙️ Key details

Company Claim Expert Response
OpenAI Astra chatbot solved decade-old math problems Mathematicians identified issues with novelty and research misconduct
OpenAI Improper attribution of work Tristan Buckmaster suggested work was stolen

💡 Why it matters

  • Cybersecurity experts characterize the hacking incidents as failures by OpenAI to adopt basic security practices rather than evidence of “rogue” models.
  • A statement signed by hundreds of professionals indicates that technology companies face commercial incentives to overstate the capabilities of their products.
  • Jacob Coxon, an engineer who departed from Anthropic, claimed that the company and OpenAI are racing toward self-improving superintelligence.
  • There is public concern regarding the industry’s focus on future, hypothetical “superintelligent” machines, which critics suggest distracts from current issues such as plagiarism, lack of consent in training data, and environmental activism against data centers.

#Anthropic #OpenAI #AIethics #Cybersecurity

Source: Don’t be fooled by this summer of AI hype

item.title: Amazon Blocks Meta's Muse AI Agent From Shopping on Its Platform
item.description:
Amazon Blocks Meta’s Muse AI Agent From Shopping on Its Platform

Amazon has blocked Meta’s Muse AI agent from shopping on its e-commerce platform on behalf of users. Users began seeing a popup message on Sunday stating that “continued access by an unauthorized AI agent violates Amazon’s Conditions of Use, to which our customers have agreed.”

⚙️ Key details

Amazon has cited several reasons for the block, including:

  • Lack of Notification: Meta did not notify Amazon that Muse would access its store.
  • Security and Privacy: Amazon expressed concerns over Muse failing to identify itself while browsing and seemingly capturing customer credentials.
  • Operational Transparency: An unnamed Amazon spokesperson told GeekWire, “We think it’s fairly straightforward that third-party applications that offer to make purchases on behalf of customers from other businesses should operate openly and respect service provider decisions about whether or not to participate."

🔍 Overview

While Meta stated at Muse’s launch earlier this month that the agent cannot see card payment information or secure login details, the agent was previously used during testing to successfully purchase tank tops from Amazon. Additionally, some privacy concerns have emerged since launch, including reports that Muse can see the contents of user messages without the necessary access permission enabled.

💡 Why it matters

This move is part of a broader effort by Amazon to keep customers shopping directly with the retailer and fend off competition from rival agentic AI services. Other related actions include:

  • Legal Action: In November of last year, Amazon sued Perplexity to keep its platform out of the Comet shopping experience, though a judge sided with Perplexity in August.
  • Data Limitation: Since July, Amazon confirmation emails have become sparse, omitting product images and specific item names to limit information being mined by external AI services.

#Meta #Amazon #MuseAI #AIAgents #Ecommerce

Source: Amazon doesn’t trust Meta’s Muse AI agent

item.title: RAND proposes US strategy to navigate uncertain transition to superintelligence
item.description:
RAND proposes US strategy to navigate uncertain transition to superintelligence

RAND has published a lengthy paper outlining strategies for the US to secure geopolitical advantage while navigating the uncertain path toward superintelligence. Because the future of AI development remains unpredictable, the report argues that the US should prioritize a “Freedom of Action” strategy to maintain options for ensuring both national advantage and human survival.

🧩 The Freedom of Action Strategy

To maintain this strategic flexibility, the report identifies four core pillars:

  • Build a human-AI ecosystem: Invest in AI safety, develop tools for human agency, share technology benefits, prepare for societal disruption, and shape ecosystem incentives.
  • Build an AI-security architecture: Gain visibility into frontier AI systems and compute, create technology to verify agreements, and build regulatory expertise.
  • Adapt legacy national security enterprises: Overhaul institutions to capitalize on AI capabilities and manage associated changes.
  • Invest in capacity: Provide decision-makers with information, diffuse positive AI uses, create crisis-response “break-glass” plans, and increase AI literacy.

⚙️ Strategic Archetypes

RAND classifies potential US approaches into seven strategies across three families:

Strategy Family Strategy Name Description
Coexistence Dominance US leads AI development and suppresses others.
Coexistence Co-Development US leads a consortium to co-develop safe superintelligence with shared governance.
Coexistence Preparedness US mobilizes efforts via voluntary commitments and phased deployment.
Denial Moratorium US pursues a verifiable global halt to development above specific thresholds.
Denial Deterrence US halts its own frontier development and uses national power to stop foreign programs.
Denial Continuity of Society US creates hardened, self-sustaining settlements to ensure survival.
Acceleration Acceleration Relies on markets and rapid iteration to produce safety as a byproduct of utility.

💡 Why it matters

The report emphasizes that effective AI strategy requires significant financial investment, even if that spending is primarily focused on preserving optionality. Currently, the US appears to favor an “acceleration” approach, which the report compares to focusing solely on engine power while neglecting essential safety features like brakes, headlights, or seatbelts.

#AI #RAND #NationalSecurity #Strategy

Source: Import AI 473: The US’s superintelligence strategy; human brain in a mouse skull; and machine hermeneutics

item.title: Hollywood unions lock in AI guardrails as tech firms urge industry slowdown
item.description:
Hollywood unions lock in AI guardrails as tech firms urge industry slowdown

Hollywood unions and writers have secured enforceable guardrails for generative AI in entertainment, while heads of major AI companies are calling for an industry‑wide slowdown.

🔍 Overview

  • AI models that generate digital facsimiles of actors and replicate traditional filmmaking tools “pose a threat to some human jobs.”
  • The AI tools used in entertainment production differ from the AI systems that have sparked recent whistleblowing and apocalyptic declarations.
  • Anthropic alignment lead Evan Hubinger warned the technology could “kill all humans” within the next decade.

🛡️ Union Negotiations

  • SAG‑AFTRA chief negotiator Duncan Crabtree‑Ireland said the union recognized early on how AI could impact its members’ livelihoods.
  • “We bargained for and achieved enforceable, meaningful guardrails around how this technology can be implemented by the major employers in our industry,” Crabtree‑Ireland explained.
  • The guardrails do not include companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google directly, but do cover all U.S. entertainment content creators.
  • WGAE executive director Sam Wheeler condemned the “tech oligarchs pushing AI on our society.”
  • The WGAE has long warned that unregulated artificial intelligence poses an existential threat to workers, to our democracy, and to the world.
  • Guild members have bargained meaningful AI protections into their contracts; in 2023 WGA members spent 148 days on strike before studios agreed to real safeguards for film and television writers.

⚙️ Industry Response

  • Hollywood unions’ fight for strict rules around generative AI did not stop the entertainment industry from embracing AI.
  • Alliance of Motion Picture and Television Producers (AMPTP) has been reluctant to adopt demands such as requiring studios to gain permission and compensate actors for AI‑generated replicas.
  • Crabtree‑Ireland noted that without the principle of compensation, “the economic incentive to use replication and to replace human performances would have been much stronger” and would have resulted in “a much greater and faster adoption of digital replication.”

🚨 Risks & Concerns

  • AI‑generated digital replicas threaten certain acting and filmmaking jobs.
  • Prominent AI leaders (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, X) have called for an industry‑wide slowdown on the technology’s development.

🏛️ Political Context

  • President Donald Trump dismissed AI concerns as overreactions.
  • Some other U.S. politicians have felt pressured to take legislative action.

📊 Companies Calling for a Slowdown

Company Action
Anthropic Called for industry‑wide slowdown
OpenAI Called for industry‑wide slowdown
Google DeepMind Called for industry‑wide slowdown
X Called for industry‑wide slowdown

#AI #Hollywood #Unions #GenAI #Slowdown

Source: What Hollywood thinks about existential AI warnings

item.title: Industry Leaders and Historians Call for AI Regulation and Caution
item.description:
Industry Leaders and Historians Call for AI Regulation and Caution

Prominent technology executives and researchers are advocating for the regulation of artificial intelligence, citing long-term risks and the need for proactive government oversight.

💡 Why it matters

Concerns regarding autonomous systems date back several decades:

  • In 1863, Samuel Butler warned that intelligent self-replicating machines could replace humans.
  • In 1951, Alan Turing stated that undying machines would eventually “take control” and “outstrip our feeble powers.”
  • In 2000, Bill Joy described self-replicating robots as potentially more dangerous than nuclear weapons.

⚙️ Key details

Various industry leaders have called for specific regulatory actions and precautions:

Person Position/Affiliation Stated View or Action
Elon Musk X CEO / OpenAI Investor Called AI “potentially more dangerous than nukes” and said we must be “proactive about regulation instead of reactive.”
Sundar Pichai Google CEO Stated “there is no question in my mind that artificial intelligence needs to be regulated.”
Brad Smith Microsoft President Opened the door to voluntary regulation in a speech at the Brookings Institution.
Mark Zuckerberg Meta Founder Suggested his company should be regulated following the Cambridge Analytica scandal.
Eric Horvitz Microsoft Chief Scientific Officer Led researchers in 2009 to consider policies to constrain behaviors of autonomous systems.

Additionally, a letter published by the Future of Life Institute and signed by Musk, among others, stated that if a pause on AI cannot be enacted quickly, “governments should step in and institute a moratorium.”

#AI #Regulation #TechPolicy #ArtificialIntelligence

Source: A brief history of AI executives calling for regulation

item.title: President Trump Calls Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang During All-In Summit
item.description:
President Trump Calls Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang During All-In Summit

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang received a phone call from President Trump while onstage at the All-In Podcast’s All-In Summit on Monday. Huang placed the president on speakerphone to address the live audience.

🔍 Overview

During the live call, President Trump addressed concerns regarding the future of artificial intelligence. He described recent fears about AI development as a “hoax” and stated that “the robots will not be taking over.”

⚙️ Key details

  • President Trump’s comments followed an essay by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, which advocated for slowing AI development and increasing government coordination.
  • In response to the discourse, President Trump stated that he intends to push back against the current narrative surrounding AI risks.
  • The president also remarked on the economic impact of data centers, claiming they have turned struggling communities into wealthy ones.

💡 Why it matters

Following the president’s statements, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang commented on the future of the industry:

Participant Stance on AI Future
President Trump The robots will not be taking over
Jensen Huang We’re going to make sure that everybody wins in the AI race in America

Huang further stated that he intends for every industry, company, state, and individual to benefit from the AI race in America.

#Nvidia #AI #JensenHuang #TechPolicy #AllInSummit

Source: Jensen Huang puts Trump on speakerphone onstage to announce robots won’t take over the world
